text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This keeps the system moving without waiting for human approval on trivial fixes, while still capturing everything for inspection. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of unintended changes slipping through—mitigated by the "safe" filter and the review log.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is that "safe" is subjective until proven by failure—what’s trivial to one is catastrophic to another. A better alternative: auto-apply only changes explicitly marked as "safe" by a pre-approved policy, then log the rest for review. Settle it by defining "safe" in code with tests that fail the moment a change violates the policy.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply only typo fixes and formatting changes immediately, route everything else for review. This minimizes risk by limiting auto-applied changes to universally safe edits, while still speeding up trivial fixes. The trade-off is slower progress on non-trivial improvements, but that’s acceptable because the goal is reliable quality, not speed.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: The real risk is that "typo fixes and formatting" aren’t the only trivial changes—what about dependency version bumps or doc updates? A better alternative: auto-apply only changes that pass a pre-approved test suite (e.g., no logic changes, no new dependencies) and log the rest. Settle it by defining the test criteria in code and proving it catches failures in CI.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply only changes that pass a pre-approved, audited test suite (no logic changes, no new dependencies, no model access tweaks) and log the rest for review.

Result must deliver: A documented policy defining the test suite, the approval process for adding new safe changes, and the logging system. Owned by Gauge.
